subject: Overlay MTU mismatch + BGP policy translation - hybrid egress triage
messages:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@acme-corp.com>

Cc: netops@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent egress failures between DC-East and OnPrem 2

Hi Rohan,

Since last night we've been observing intermittent failures where application traffic from OnPrem-2 to our DC-East egress times out every ~10-15 minutes for ~30-90s. When the team disables jumbo frames on the overlay (MTU 1500 enforced) the problem goes away immediately.

Attached is a short packet capture from the customer-facing firewall showing repeated ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages and some retransmits. We also noticed that some flows appear to have their source port rewritten inconsistently when passing through the transit NAT appliance — causing sessions to fail intermittently.

Can you and your networking team take a look? We're on-call for a maintenance window this Thursday (Jun 18) 02:00-03:00 UTC if a config change is required.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Jones
NetOps Lead, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures between DC-East and OnPrem 2

Hi Alice — thanks for the capture and heads up.

Quick read: the ICMP "fragmentation needed" suggests an MTU mismatch somewhere between the overlay endpoint and the physical egress path. The inconsistent source-port rewriting you mentioned could be a separate NAT device (transit NAT) not honoring ephemeral port preservation for large packets that get fragmented, which would explain session resets when fragments arrive out of order.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa / Karthik: can you pull the BGP neighbor and interface MTU on the two egress devices (DC-East edge + OnPrem-2 transit) and check whether any overlay devices perform on-path encapsulation (GRE/VXLAN) with larger headers?
- Alice: can you confirm whether the transit NAT appliance is configured with any port randomization / port translation policies (or a firewall that reassembles fragments)?

If we confirm MTU mismatch, short-term mitigation is MSS clamping on the edge + allow fragmented packets in the security group for the maintenance window. Long-term we should negotiate or align overlay MTU and ensure the NAT preserves ports for fragmented flows.

I'll hold time in our schedule for Thu 02:00 UTC.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures between DC-East and OnPrem 2

Hi all — quick lab reproduction and notes.

What we did:
- Replayed the attached pcap through a VXLAN tunnel + transit NAT appliance in our testbed.
- Captured traffic on both sides of the NAT and on the overlay endpoint.

Findings:
- VXLAN adds ~50 bytes of overhead; OnPrem-2 had MTU 1500 on the physical interface while the overlay endpoint was configured to assume MTU 1550 (misaligned). That leads to PMTUD problems and ICMP "fragmentation needed" replies that many middleboxes drop.
- Transit NAT was configured to perform ephemeral-port randomization (policy for symmetric NAT). When fragments cross the NAT and the NAT reassigns ephemeral ports on later fragments, the reassembled stream fails and session state in the firewall is inconsistent.
- Security group on DC-East currently drops fragments by default (SG rule set disallows fragment flags) — fragments that do make it through are sometimes allowed and sometimes dropped depending on reorder, producing the intermittent pattern.

Proposed short-term plan for Thu 02:00 UTC window (safe, reversible):
1) Apply MSS clamping on DC-East egress interface to 1280 (covers overlay headers).
2) Add temporary SG allow rule for IPv4 fragments for the Acme subnet range (with tight scope and 1-hour TTL).
3) Disable ephemeral-port randomization on the transit NAT (set to preserve original ephemeral port mapping) — if that's not possible, add a stateful reassembly helper on the NAT.

Rollback steps:
- Remove MSS clamp and SG rule, reenable the NAT policy. We can script these and test rollbacks in the maintenance window.

I can prepare the exact CLI snippets if we get a green light.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Post-change summary: maintenance window results and next steps

TL;DR: Changes applied during the 02:00 UTC window resolved the intermittent egress failures.

What we changed (applied in order, validated each step):
- Applied MSS clamp on DC-East egress interface to 1280 (CLI snippet applied).
- Added temporary security group rule allowing IPv4 fragments for the Acme v4 space (scoped to transit/egress IPs).
- Updated transit NAT policy to preserve ephemeral source ports for fragments (immediate change on the device).

Validation:
- We replayed the original pcap and confirmed no ICMP "fragmentation needed" responses and no session resets after the NAT.
- Production metrics: retransmit spikes dropped to baseline within 3 minutes. No application errors reported by Acme after 10 minutes of monitoring.

Attachments: post_change_summary.txt (contains CLI snippets used and timestamps).

Recommended long-term remediation (tracked in NET-4821):
- Align overlay MTU negotiation: implement a discovery/advertise step so endpoints auto-adjust when underlying path overhead changes.
- Ensure NAT devices preserve ephemeral ports for fragmented flows or perform reassembly before translation.
- Update our onboarding checklist to include overlay MTU checks and NAT port behavior for any private deployment.

Rollback note: We kept the temporary SG rule enabled for 1 hour and then removed it as planned. MSS clamp was left for 24 hours while we monitor; we will remove it after NET-4821 completion if we push the overlay MTU negotiation fix.

Thanks to the Acme team for quick coordination. Follow-up: I'll create a short runbook with the CLI snippets and rollback automation and link it on the NET-4821 ticket.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
